session_summary: We caught up about the weekend and the open-water swim on Saturday. You described the race conditions in good detail and we worked on past-tense narration. We also talked about a stressful project deadline and practiced softer ways to complain about work.

learning_items.meaning: to actually complete something you said you would do
learning_items.example: I signed up for the race, so now I have to follow through.

learning_items.meaning: a natural way to say you are extremely busy
learning_items.example: Sorry I didn't reply — I've been swamped at work this week.
learning_items.note: casual; fine with colleagues, avoid in formal writing

learning_items.meaning: to finish work by the required time
learning_items.example: We barely met the deadline on Friday.

learning_items.meaning: a new burst of energy after feeling tired
learning_items.example: Halfway through the swim I got my second wind.

corrections.original: I went to swimming pool yesterday morning.
corrections.corrected: I went to the swimming pool yesterday morning.

corrections.explanation: 'Choppy' is the natural word, and 'water' takes a singular verb.

corrections.original: I didn't went to the office on Friday.
corrections.corrected: I didn't go to the office on Friday.

recurring_mistakes.description: Dropping 'the' before specific places (pool, office, gym).

pronunciation_notes.note: First vowel is /ɑ/ as in 'hot', not /oʊ/.

shadowing: I signed up for the race, so now I have to follow through.
The water was really choppy, but I got my second wind halfway.
I've been swamped, but we barely met the deadline.
next_session_focus: Past-tense narration of a full story without switching to present tense.
